title: White chocolate truffles
subtitle: white chocolate ganache rolled into smooth balls and finished in desiccated coconut or icing sugar
excerpt: White chocolate truffles are made from a ganache of white chocolate and cream, set in the fridge until firm, then scooped and rolled into balls. They can be coated in desiccated coconut, dusted with icing sugar, or dipped in melted white chocolate. The finished truffles set hard on the outside and stay soft inside.
sourceNotes: White chocolate ganache truffles are a modern confection that became popular as white chocolate became widely available in Europe during the 1970s and 1980s. The truffle format is adapted from French dark chocolate ganache truffles, which date from the late nineteenth century.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze uncoated in a single layer for up to 2 months. Coat after thawing.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well. Use a larger bowl for the ganache.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keeps refrigerated for up to 2 weeks. Serve at room temperature.

content.text: White chocolate truffles are a very soft ganache, set firm in the fridge, shaped into balls, and coated in coconut or icing sugar. The ganache is warm cream poured over chopped white chocolate, stirred until smooth, then chilled until firm. The tricky part is keeping your hands cool when rolling so the ganache does not melt.
Put the chopped white chocolate in a heatproof bowl. Bring the cream just to the boil in a small saucepan. Pour over the chocolate immediately and leave for 1 minute without stirring.
Stir slowly from the centre outward until the chocolate has melted completely and the ganache is smooth and glossy. Add the butter and vanilla. Stir until the butter is fully incorporated.
Pour into a shallow dish. Press cling film directly onto the surface. Refrigerate for 2 hours until firm enough to scoop and hold its shape.

Spread the coconut or sifted icing sugar on a plate. Scoop the ganache with a melon baller or teaspoon. Drop each portion into the coating and roll quickly between cool palms into a smooth ball. Place on a tray lined with baking paper.
Refrigerate the finished truffles for 30 minutes to firm the coating. Serve at room temperature.

attrs.problem: Ganache stays liquid and does not set firm after chilling
attrs.avoid: Avoid too much cream relative to chocolate; white chocolate sets more softly than dark.
attrs.fix: Refrigerate for an additional hour. If still too soft, melt in an extra 50 g of white chocolate, stir through, and chill again.

attrs.problem: Ganache separates into grainy lumps and liquid
attrs.avoid: Avoid stirring the hot cream immediately after pouring; this can cause the chocolate to seize.
attrs.fix: Let the hot cream sit on the chocolate for a full minute before stirring. If it has seized, add 1 tablespoon of warm cream and stir vigorously from the centre outward.
